ar-QA.englishGloss: Natural sea pearls (traditionally called qimash in Gulf pearl trade)
ar-QA.culturalNote: In historic Qatari and Gulf usage, natural pearls were affectionately termed qimash alongside lulu.

ar-QA.englishGloss: Traditional flat-transom wooden dhow with a vertical bow used along Qatar's coast
ar-QA.culturalNote: Built and maintained by master shipwrights (qallaf) along Doha Bay.
Uses palm-fiber rope, wooden mallets, and shark-liver/plant oils to seal hull planks.

ar-QA.englishGloss: Pearl merchant who grades pearls by size, luster, and weight
ar-QA.culturalNote: Uses brass sieves (tasa) and mithqal scales in fair harbor exchange.

ar-QA.englishGloss: Qatari coastal folktale of a kind young woman aided by a magical sea fish (Folklore)
ar-QA.culturalNote: Explicitly classified as folklore pending regional variant corroboration.

ar-QA.englishGloss: The joyous coastal homecoming marking the safe return of pearl boats to shore
ar-QA.culturalNote: Celebrates family reunion, gratitude, and shoreline welcome signals.

ar-AE.englishGloss: Traditional wind-catcher tower that funnels cool breezes into courtyard rooms
ar-AE.culturalNote: Found in historic coastal quarters of Dubai and Sharjah.

ar-AE.englishGloss: Gravity-fed water channel irrigating inland oases like Al Ain
ar-AE.culturalNote: Documented at UNESCO World Heritage Site #1343 in Al Ain.

ar-AE.englishGloss: Natural saltwater creek or inlet sheltering trading dhows
ar-AE.culturalNote: Central to coastal settlements in Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi.

ar-AE.englishGloss: Polaris (the North Star), used by Gulf navigators to find northern bearings
ar-AE.culturalNote: Paired with southern star Suhayl (Canopus) in traditional star compasses.

ar-AE.englishGloss: Traditional Emirati hand-braided textile craft woven on a kajooja cushion

ar-AE.msaEquivalent: أهلاً وسهلاً بكم في كل وقت
ar-AE.englishGloss: Warm Emirati greeting meaning "Welcome at this very hour"

ar-KW.msaEquivalent: سفينة شراعية كويتية ذات مقدمة ومؤخرة مدببة
ar-KW.englishGloss: Large double-ended Kuwaiti dhow famous for long-distance cargo and water transport
ar-KW.culturalNote: A national symbol of Kuwaiti maritime craftsmanship.

ar-KW.englishGloss: Dhow captain responsible for navigation, crew welfare, and fair harbor trade
ar-KW.culturalNote: Central leadership role in historic Kuwaiti seafaring.

ar-KW.msaEquivalent: شخصية أسطورية بحرية في الفلكلور الخليجي
ar-KW.englishGloss: Legendary sea figure from Gulf maritime folklore associated with night winds and waves
ar-KW.culturalNote: Explicitly presented as folklore; interpreted gently through natural harbor acoustics for younger players.

ar-KW.englishGloss: Maritime vocalist who leads call-and-response work songs (nahma) aboard a dhow
ar-KW.culturalNote: Kept crew morale high and synchronized heavy rope-pulling tasks.

ar-KW.englishGloss: Tidal stone-walled harbor basin sheltering dhows along the Kuwait City shore
ar-KW.culturalNote: Historic examples include Naq'at Al-Shamlan along Kuwait Bay.

ar-KW.englishGloss: Master shipwright skilled in shaping and caulking wooden dhow hulls
ar-KW.culturalNote: Kuwaiti qallaf guilds built some of the largest Boom dhows in the Gulf.

ar-SA.englishGloss: Classical Arabic ode structured with balanced meter and rhyme
ar-SA.culturalNote: Central poetic form of the Arabian Peninsula from pre-Islamic times to today.

ar-SA.msaEquivalent: القصائد السبع أو العشر المشهورة في الشعر الجاهلي
ar-SA.englishGloss: Celebrated anthology of pre-Islamic Arabic odes, including the poem of Antarah ibn Shaddad
ar-SA.culturalNote: The story that they were hung in gold letters on the Kaaba is explicitly noted as a famous, debated literary tradition.

ar-SA.englishGloss: Desert caravan traveling together for mutual safety, shared water, and trade
ar-SA.culturalNote: Connected Arabian oases such as Najd, Al-Ula/Hegra, and coastal ports.

ar-SA.msaEquivalent: مكان الجلوس والضيافة وتبادل الحديث والشعر
ar-SA.englishGloss: Traditional sitting room or courtyard space for welcoming guests, sharing poetry, and community counsel
ar-SA.culturalNote: UNESCO-recognized cultural space across Saudi Arabia and the Gulf.

ar-SA.msaEquivalent: نسيج البادية التقليدي ذو الزخارف الهندسية
ar-SA.englishGloss: Traditional horizontal-loom geometric weaving crafted from desert wool
ar-SA.culturalNote: Inscribed by UNESCO (2020) as Intangible Cultural Heritage.

ar-SA.englishGloss: Moral courage, magnanimity, keeping one's word, and protecting the dignity of others
ar-SA.culturalNote: Core ethical ideal celebrated in Antarah's poetry—rooted in character rather than force.

ar-OM.englishGloss: Gravity-fed water channels carrying mountain spring or groundwater to villages and gardens
ar-OM.culturalNote: Five representative Omani aflaj are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List (#1207).

ar-OM.englishGloss: Trusted community water master who coordinates falaj maintenance and fair time-shares
ar-OM.culturalNote: Uses sundials (lamad) by day and guiding stars by night.

ar-OM.englishGloss: Traditional 30-minute time unit of irrigation water (48 athar in a 24-hour day)
ar-OM.culturalNote: Ensures water is shared by measured time rather than upstream monopoly.

ar-OM.englishGloss: Aromatic frankincense resin harvested from Boswellia sacra trees in Dhofar
Traditional waterproof Omani mortar used to line falaj channels and cisterns
ar-OM.culturalNote: Prepared by firing local clay and lime.

ar-OM.msaEquivalent: نقطة السقيا الأولى في مدخل القرية
ar-OM.englishGloss: The first open-air basin where a falaj enters the village, reserved for clean drinking water
ar-OM.culturalNote: Demonstrates community hygiene and water-priority engineering.

ar-BH.englishGloss: Bronze Age civilization and trade hub centered on Bahrain (Qal'at al-Bahrain, UNESCO #1192)
ar-BH.culturalNote: Known archaeologically from circular seals and city strata, and separately in Mesopotamian mythology.

ar-BH.englishGloss: Ancient Harbour and Capital of Dilmun archaeological tell on Bahrain's northern coast

ar-BH.msaEquivalent: نبع ماء عذب تحت قاع البحر
ar-BH.englishGloss: Freshwater submarine spring bubbling up beneath the salty sea around Bahrain
ar-BH.culturalNote: Connected to the name Al-Bahrain ("The Two Seas": sweet water and salt water).

ar-BH.englishGloss: Compartmented wooden chest used by 19th–20th century Muharraq pearl merchants
ar-BH.culturalNote: Part of the Muharraq Pearling Path (UNESCO #1364).

ar-BH.englishGloss: Cooperative Bahraini embroidery craft where weavers braid metallic threads together
Archaeological layers (stratigraphy) showing different historical time periods in order
ar-BH.culturalNote: Prevents collapsing ancient Dilmun and modern pearling into a single era.
